entries.title: John 11:1
segments: Now a man named Lazarus, of Bethany, was lying ill; he belonged to the same village as Mary and her sister Martha.

entries.title: John 11:2
segments: This Mary, whose brother Lazarus was ill, was the Mary who anointed the Master with perfume, and wiped his feet with her hair.

entries.title: John 11:3
segments: The sisters, therefore, sent this message to Jesus--'Master, your friend is ill';

entries.title: John 11:4
segments: And, when Jesus heard it, he said: "This illness is not to end in death, but is to redound to the honor of God, in order that the Son of God may be honored through it."

entries.title: John 11:5
segments: Jesus loved Martha and her sister, and Lazarus.

entries.title: John 11:6
segments: Yet, when he heard of the illness of Lazarus, he still stayed two days in the place where he was.

entries.title: John 11:7
segments: Then, after that, he said to his disciples: "Let us go to Judea again."

entries.title: John 11:8
segments: "Rabbi," they replied, "the Jews were but just now seeking to stone you; and are you going there again?"

entries.title: John 11:9
segments: "Are not there twelve hours in the day?" answered Jesus. "If a man walks about in the day-time, he does not stumble, because he can see the light of the sun;

entries.title: John 11:10
segments: But, if he walks about at night, he stumbles, because he has not the light."

entries.title: John 11:11
segments: And, when he had said this, he added: "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep; but I am going that I may wake him."

entries.title: John 11:12
segments: "If he has fallen asleep, Master, he will get well," said the disciples.

entries.title: John 11:13
segments: But Jesus meant that he was dead; they, however, supposed that he was speaking of natural sleep.

entries.title: John 11:14
segments: Then he said to them plainly: "Lazarus is dead;

entries.title: John 11:15
segments: And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, so that you may learn to believe in me. But let us go to him."

entries.title: John 11:16
segments: At this, Thomas, who was called 'The Twin,' said to his fellow-disciples: "Let us go too, so that we may die with him."

entries.title: John 11:17
segments: When Jesus reached the place, he found that Lazarus had been four days in the tomb already.

entries.title: John 11:18
segments: Bethany being only about two miles from Jerusalem,

entries.title: John 11:19
segments: A number of the Jews had come there to condole with Martha and Mary on their brother's death.

entries.title: John 11:20
segments: When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet him; but Mary sat quietly at home.

entries.title: John 11:21
segments: "Master," Martha said to Jesus, "if you had been here, my brother would not have died.

entries.title: John 11:22
segments: Even now, I know that God will grant you whatever you ask him."

entries.title: John 11:23
segments: "Your brother shall rise to life," said Jesus.

entries.title: John 11:24
segments: "I know that he will," replied Martha, "in the resurrection at the Last Day."

entries.title: John 11:25
segments: "I am the Resurrection and the Life," said Jesus. "He that believes in me shall live, though he die;

entries.title: John 11:26
segments: And he who lives and believes in me shall never die. Do you believe this?"

entries.title: John 11:27
segments: "Yes Master," she answered; "I have learned to believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, 'who was to come' into the world."

entries.title: John 11:28
segments: After saying this, Martha went and called her sister Mary, and whispered: "The Teacher is here, and is asking for you."

entries.title: John 11:29
segments: As soon as Mary heard that, she got up quickly, and went to meet him.

entries.title: John 11:30
segments: Jesus had not then come into the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met him.

entries.title: John 11:31
segments: So the Jews, who were in the house with Mary, condoling with her, when they saw her get up quickly and go out, followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep there.

entries.title: John 11:32
segments: When Mary came where Jesus was and saw him, she threw herself at his feet. "Master," she exclaimed, "if you had been here, my brother would not have died!"

entries.title: John 11:33
segments: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping also, he groaned deeply, and was greatly distressed.

entries.title: John 11:34
segments: "Where have you buried him?" he asked. "Come and see, Master," they answered.

entries.title: John 11:35
segments: Jesus burst into tears.

entries.title: John 11:36
segments: "How he must have loved him!" the Jews exclaimed;

entries.title: John 11:37
segments: But some of them said: "Could not this man, who gave sight to the blind man, have also prevented Lazarus from dying?"

entries.title: John 11:38
segments: Again groaning inwardly, Jesus came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against the mouth of it.

entries.title: John 11:39
segments: "Move the stone away," said Jesus. "Master," said Martha, the sister of the dead man, "by this time the smell must be offensive, for this is the fourth day since his death."

entries.title: John 11:40
segments: "Did not I tell you," replied Jesus, "that, if you would believe in me, you should see the glory of God?"

entries.title: John 11:41
segments: So they moved the stone away; and Jesus, with uplifted eyes, said: "Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard my prayer;

entries.title: John 11:42
segments: I know that thou always headrest me; but I say this for the sake of the people standing near, so that they may believe that thou has sent me as thy Messenger."

entries.title: John 11:43
segments: Then, after saying this, Jesus called in a loud voice: "Lazarus! come out!"

entries.title: John 11:44
segments: The dead man came out, wrapped hand and foot in a winding- sheet; his face, too, had been wrapped in a cloth. "Set him free," said Jesus, "and let him go."

entries.title: John 11:45
segments: In consequence of this, many of the Jews, who had come to visit Mary and had seen what Jesus did, learned to believe in him.

entries.title: John 11:46
segments: Some of them, however, went to the Pharisees, and told them what he had done.

entries.title: John 11:47
segments: Upon this the Chief Priests and the Pharisees called a meeting of the High Council, and said: "What are we to do, now that this man is giving so many signs?

entries.title: John 11:48
segments: If we let him alone as we are doing, every one will believe in him; and the Romans will come and will take from us both our City and our Nationality."

entries.title: John 11:49
segments: One of them, however, Caiaphas, who was High Priest that year, said to them:

entries.title: John 11:50
segments: "You are utterly mistaken. You do not consider that it is better for you that one man should die for the people, rather than the whole nation should be destroyed."

entries.title: John 11:51
segments: Now he did not say this of his own accord; but, as High Priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was to die for the nation--

entries.title: John 11:52
segments: And not for the nation only, but also that he might unite in one body the Children of God now scattered far and wide.

entries.title: John 11:53
segments: So from that day they plotted to put Jesus to death.

entries.title: John 11:54
segments: In consequence of this, Jesus did not go about publicly among the Jews any more, but left that neighborhood, and went into the country bordering on the Wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, where he stayed with his disciples.

entries.title: John 11:55
segments: But the Jewish Festival of the Passover was near; and many people had gone up from the country to Jerusalem, for their 'purification,' before the Festival began.

entries.title: John 11:56
segments: So they looked for Jesus there, and said to one another, as they stood in the Temple Courts: "What do you think? Do you think he will come to the Festival?"

entries.title: John 11:57
segments: The Chief Priests and the Pharisees had already issued orders that, if any one learned where Jesus was, he should give information, so that they might arrest him.
